title: Leia George
text:
CARE · CURIOSITY · CONNECTION


I’m Leia George. My interests bring together clinical care, mental health research, and the science of how we heal.
I am a Research Project Coordinator in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Health at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, where I work with Drs. Nicholas Allan and Melanie Bozzay on NIH-funded research, including the Advanced Resilience and Coping Study (ARC; R01MH136286) and Anxiety Sensitivity Treatment to Reduce Anxiety in Alzheimer’s (ASTRA; R01AG077569). My broader research interests lie at the intersection of clinical psychology, suicide prevention, and mental health interventions, with an emphasis on understanding psychological processes and improving clinical care.
I earned my Master of Science in Medical Physiology and Biophysics from Case Western Reserve University and my bachelor’s degree from Baylor University.
Beyond research, I am passionate about mental health advocacy, social justice, and addressing structural barriers to equitable care. I value collaborative, accessible, and inclusive science that reflects the diversity of the populations it aims to serve. I am always happy to connect with fellow researchers and potential collaborators!
